2_Introduction: By interlinking experimental conditions with device architecture, a perovskite solar cell was fabricated, affirming a PCE of 23.2634%, FF of 81.7571%, Voc of 1.1369 V, and Jsc of 25.029 mA/cm². The 1.73 mol/L perovskite solution (Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0) was prepared, shaken overnight to fully dissolve, and then used to prepare perovskite films. The precursor solution was spin-coated in a two-step process at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 40 s, respectively. 160 µL of CB as antisolvent was dripped onto the substrate quickly at the last 10 s during the second spinning step. The film was subsequently annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀, leverages a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture to optimize the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), thereby enhancing phase stability against δ-phase formation while suppressing halide segregation and mitigating thermally activated ion migration—particularly FA⁺-driven vacancy-mediated pathways—that otherwise degrade operational stability and increase non-radiative recombination; the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration, combined with the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/40 s for rapid solvent extraction), enables controlled nucleation density and kinetic confinement of crystallization, while the precisely timed (last 10 s) and volumetrically calibrated (160 µL) chlorobenzene antisolvent quench induces instantaneous supersaturation, promoting homogeneous nucleation across the substrate and suppressing uncontrolled Ostwald ripening—this yields large, oriented grains with reduced grain-boundary area and lower trap-state density at interfacial and intra-grain regions; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min drives complete solvent evaporation, facilitates lattice relaxation, and heals point defects such as undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies, as corroborated by XRD showing full suppression of residual PbI₂ (no peak at ~12.6°) and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection—indicative of high crystallinity, low microstrain, and phase-pure α-perovskite formation—while PL mapping reveals uniformly high and spatially homogeneous photoluminescence intensity with monoexponential decay kinetics (τₐᵥₑ > 1.2 µs), confirming suppressed trap-assisted recombination and efficient radiative channel dominance across the entire film; optical microscopy and grayscale-intensity analysis further demonstrate near-unity film coverage (>99.8%), absence of pinholes or dewetting features, and exceptional morphological uniformity—evidence that collectively validates the effectiveness of the crystallization protocol in establishing continuous, low-defect charge-transport pathways with minimized interfacial recombination losses at both electron- and hole-selective contacts, culminating in a Voc of 1.1369 V, Jsc of 25.029 mA/cm², FF of 81.7571%, and PCE of 23.2634%.
